title: Hallway mediator sequencer for tool pipelines with tame recursion
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Multi-tool chains frequently cause unbounded recursion and KV pollution when tool outputs are naively injected into the conversational context or KV cache. This is exacerbated by streaming responses (partial outputs) and heterogeneous tool interfaces (some return structured JSON, others free text).

Goal: Implement a sequencer/middleware (codenamed 'Hallway mediator') that coordinates multi-tool invocation pipelines to enable: 1) safe incremental injection of tool results, 2) bounded recursion/loop guards, 3) streaming-compatible function/tool calling, and 4) a compatibility layer that normalizes varied tool outputs into a structured, verifiable form. The solution should be pluggable into the existing orchestrator and respect latency and SLO constraints for host/Dedicated modes.
acceptance_criteria: Sequencer can run a chain of 1..N tool invocations with a per-chain recursion budget and hard stop at budget exhaustion
Tool outputs are quarantined in a KV 'staging' namespace until sanitizer/validator approves them before global injection
Streaming tools can emit partial results that are visible to the caller while quarantined outputs are tagged as 'provisional' and cannot influence downstream tool selection until certified
Compatibility shim converts legacy plain-text tool outputs into the platform's structured output schema or attaches a deterministic parse binary so downstream components can safely consume results
End-to-end test coverage for: recursion abort, provisional streaming visibility, sanitizer rejection and rollback, and compatibility shim for at least two legacy tool interfaces
Benchmarks: median added latency per chain step < 5ms for local planner overhead; memory/KV overhead within acceptable limits under 99th percentile load
implementation_plan:
Phase 1: Implement sequencer core and chain budget. Introduce lightweight 'frame token' that travels with every invocation; token carries chain-id, step-index and remaining budget. Phase 2: KV staging layer and sanitizer hooks. Build a sanitizer interface that runs validators (schema, hallucination checks, length and token budget checks) asynchronously and returns a signed approval blob. Phase 3: Streaming integration: add provisional tags to partial stream frames and expose an API to observe provisional vs certified frames. Phase 4: Compatibility shims: create adapters for legacy tools (text->structured, csv->table) and register parsers for common legacy formats. Phase 5: Rollout behind feature flag; canary in production for selected customers, monitor rollback metrics.

Implementation notes: keep the sequencer deterministic (idempotent chain replay) by using stable chain-ids computed from request id + seed. Use an optimistic injection strategy: downstream tool selection may see provisional metadata (non-authoritative) but will not be allowed to mutate KV/global state until approval blob is present. Failure modes must bubble up cleanly to the caller with structured errors and suggested fallbacks.
engineering_notes: KV staging namespace: staging/<chain_id>/<step> with TTL tied to chain budget + 1 minute buffer

Sanitizer interface will run as sync for small checks (schema, signer) and async for heavy checks (semantic regression models). The sequencer must allow optimistic exec but enforce a final reconciliation step.
Compatibility policy: if shim fails to parse, attach original payload under 'raw_payload' and mark as 'unparsed' so downstream can choose to fallback to text-mode processing
Streaming: adopt a 'provisional' boolean in stream frames; provisional frames cannot trigger downstream tool invocations that change chain budget. Certified frames can.
notes_on_risks: Performance: adding staging/quarantine could increase median latency if sanitizer is blocking; mitigate via async certs and provisional visibility
Complexity: introduces more surface area for debugging multi-tool traces; need enhanced trace propagation and a per-chain timeline UI in Console
Compatibility: legacy tools with nondeterministic outputs may cause frequent sanitizer rejections leading to higher abort rates; we must provide clear remediation metrics and prompts to partner teams
Security: quarantined data still lives in KV; ensure access controls and TTLs are enforced to avoid leakage
